               Plaintiff,             ORDER GRANTING IN PART AND

           v.                         REQUEST TO SEAL DOCUMENTS

     NVIDIA CORPORATION,              Re: Dkt. No. 162                    
12                                                                         
               Defendant.                                                 

13                                                                         
14        On December 2, 2024, defendant NVIDIA Corporation (“NVIDIA”) filed an 
15   administrative motion to file materials under seal in connection with its opposition to plaintiff 
16   Valeo Schalter und Sensoren GMBH’s (“Valeo”) motion for a letter of request pursuant to the 
17   Hague Convention.  Dkt. No. 162.  NVIDIA seeks to seal the entirety of Exhibit A to its 
18   opposition, which consists of NVIDIA’s responses to Valeo’s Interrogatory No. 2.  Dkt. No. 162-
19   2.                                                                    
20        There is a strong presumption in favor of access by the public to judicial records and 
21   documents accompanying dispositive motions that can be overcome only by a showing of 
22   “compelling reasons supported by specific factual findings.”  Kamakana v. City & Cnty. of 
23   Honolulu, 447 F.3d 1172, 1178-79 (9th Cir. 2006) (cleaned up).  However, the presumption does 
24   not apply equally to a motion addressing matters that are only “tangentially related to the merits of 
25   a case.”  Ctr. for Auto Safety v. Chrysler Group, LLC, 809 F.3d 1092, 1101 (9th Cir. 2016).  A 
26   party seeking to seal documents or information in connection with such a motion must meet the 
27   lower “good cause” standard of Fed. R. Civ. P. 26(c).  Id. at 1098-99; Kamakana, 447 F.3d at 
   1    defenses, so the Court applies the “good cause” standard of Rule 26(c). 
   2          NVIDIA asserts that good cause supports sealing the information in Exhibit A because it 
   3    “contains information about the organization of NVIDIA’s source code, and identifies at least two 
   4  ||  specific functions in the source code.”  Dkt. No. 162-3 4] 2.  NVIDIA further asserts that Exhibit A 
   5    identifies “certain key NVIDIA employees, as well as the specific projects they have worked on.” 
   6 ||  Id. 
   7          The Court is not persuaded that good cause exists to seal the entirety of the document.  The 
   8    document contains objections to the interrogatories and high-level descriptions of NVIDIA’s 
   9    technology and the work of its employees that does not reveal any non-public information.  In 
  10  ||  particular, the individuals whose names appear on page 11 of the exhibit, including Mohammad 
  11    Moniruzzaman and Mohamed Shawki Elamir, have already been disclosed publicly.  See, e.g., 
   12  || Dkt. No. 23 9 52; Dkt. No. 152 at 1; Dkt. No. 173 at 2.  While the Court agrees that good cause 
   13    exists to the seal the names and responsibilities of NVIDIA employees whose work is not at issue 
  14 ||  for purposes of the present motion (page 9, lines 4-15 of the exhibit) and specific information 
   15  || describing NVIDIA’s work on technology improvements that have not yet been disclosed (page 
a    16    11, lines 12-14 of the exhibit), the Court finds that NVIDIA has not otherwise shown good cause 
3    17    to seal the remainder of the exhibit. 
   18          NVIDIA shall file a public redacted version of Exhibit A that conforms to this order no 
  19    later than January 24, 2025. 
  20          IT IS SO ORDERED. 
  21    Dated: January 10, 2025 
  22 

                                                       Virginia K. DeMarchi 
  24                                                    United States Magistrate Judge
